title: UPGRADE FORESIGHT AUDITOR

19.1.finding: Cache JSON files have no schema validation — type assertions mask missing fields at runtime.
evidence: src/lib/cache.ts:12 — `JSON.parse(...) as T` uses TypeScript type assertion with zero runtime validation
src/lib/cache.ts:36 — same pattern: `JSON.parse(...) as Persona[]`
src/lib/types.ts:145-155 — CachedDemoData has 8 required fields; none are optional
src/data/cache/ — 9 JSON files exist but no schema version field in any of them

If a new required field is added to WalletData (e.g. `riskScore: number`), existing cache JSON files would parse without error, but the field would be `undefined` at runtime, causing `TypeError` on property access
No Zod, Yup, io-ts, or any runtime schema validation library in package.json
19.1.impact: Adding new required fields to CachedDemoData, WalletData, Pattern, Persona, or RoastBattle types would silently break cache reads because `JSON.parse(...) as T` performs no validation. Consumers that access `.toLowerCase()`, `.map()`, or arithmetic on undefined fields crash at runtime with no clear error.
19.1.mitigation: Add a `version` field to each cache JSON file and use Zod or a simple runtime type guard in loadJson<T>() to validate shape before casting. On version mismatch, throw a clear error with migration instructions.

19.2.finding: No seed script exists and no cache regeneration path is available — the error message points to a non-existent file.
evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:127 — references `scripts/seed-demo.ts` as the cache generator
scripts/ directory — does not exist: `ls scripts/` returns ENOENT
src/lib/cache.ts:10 — error message says `Run scripts/seed-demo.ts first` but the file does not exist
src/lib/cache.ts:35-42 — loadPersonas() has a fallback path that calls generatePersona() dynamically, but only works if patterns are cached
src/lib/cache.ts:48-62 — loadRoastBattle() has a fallback that generates from roast-lines.json + personas, but roast-lines.json must already exist
No migration script, no `npm run seed`, no `npm run migrate`, no regeneration command anywhere in package.json scripts
19.2.impact: If cache data structure changes (new fields, removed fields, renamed fields), there is no way to regenerate the 9 cache JSON files. The seed script that ARCHITECTURE.md and cache.ts reference does not exist. A developer would need to manually hand-edit JSON files or reverse-engineer the expected shapes from type definitions, which is error-prone and time-consuming.
19.2.mitigation: Create scripts/seed-demo.ts that calls OnchainOS CLI and outputs cache files matching current types. Add `npm run seed` to package.json. For migration, add a `cacheVersion` constant and a `migrate-cache.ts` script that transforms old-format JSON to new-format.

19.3.finding: No API versioning exists — the frontend and API are tightly coupled with compile-time-only type safety.
evidence: src/app/api/analyze/route.ts:27,101 — uses `satisfies AnalyzeResponse` which is compile-time only; no runtime version header
No `/api/v1/` prefix on any route; paths are `/api/analyze`, `/api/persona`, `/api/compare`, `/api/roast`
grep for 'version|API_VERSION|migrat|upgrade|compat' in src/ returned 0 matches

AnalyzeResponse (types.ts:168-175) has 6 fields — if any are removed or renamed, `satisfies` catches it at build time, but if the API adds a new required field that the frontend doesn't expect, the frontend would compile fine but could fail at runtime on the response
No response envelope with version field; API responses are bare JSON objects with no `apiVersion` or `schemaVersion`
19.3.impact: Since this is a monorepo (frontend + API deploy together), the risk of version skew is low in normal operation. However: (1) if the API is ever consumed by external clients, adding/removing fields breaks them; (2) if a rollback deploys old frontend against new cached data format, the UI silently breaks; (3) no way to negotiate API version at runtime.
19.3.mitigation: Add an `apiVersion: 1` field to all API responses. Use a response envelope: `{ apiVersion: 1, data: {...} }`. For external consumption, version the URL path (`/api/v1/analyze`). Consider making new fields optional (`?`) in TypeScript so old consumers don't crash.

19.4.finding: No admin mechanism exists; deployment is blocked (Vercel unauthenticated) and there is no CI/CD pipeline.
evidence: .deploy-state.json:phase_ledger[9] — platform_deploy phase: 'PARTIAL: GitHub repo live. Vercel BLOCKED — no credentials.'
.deploy-state.json:errors[0] — 'Vercel CLI not authenticated. No credentials found.'
.deploy-state.json:project_profile.ci — false (no GitHub Actions or CI configured)
.deploy-state.json:project_profile.deploy_targets — ['vercel'] (single target, not connected)
.vercel/project.json — project linked (prj_b3PS3eS5TammYL6H8dm6049e9yy0) but never deployed
No admin panel, no auth middleware, no upgrade API endpoint, no admin route in src/app/
Single developer: dmustapha (from .deploy-state.json phase 0)
package.json scripts — only dev, build, start, lint; no deploy, no release, no promote scripts
19.4.impact: The intended upgrade path is Vercel git-push auto-deploy, but it's not connected. The actual path today is: developer manually runs `vercel login` then `vercel --prod`. There is no staging environment, no canary deploys, no rollback mechanism beyond `vercel rollback`. For a single-dev hackathon project this is acceptable, but any team expansion would need structured deploy access.
19.4.mitigation: Complete Vercel connection: run `vercel login`, connect the GitHub repo at vercel.com for auto-deploy on push to main. Add `vercel.json` with production/staging environment configs. For team scenarios, add GitHub branch protection rules and Vercel team member roles.

19.5.finding: Zero migration tests exist; cache file integrity is never validated at build time, test time, or startup.
evidence: file_search *.test.* — 0 results across the entire project
file_search *.spec.* — only Playwright E2E tests (stress-browser.spec.ts), no data migration tests
src/lib/cache.ts:9-13 — loadJson<T>() has no validation: fs.existsSync check only, then blind JSON.parse + cast
No test that verifies cache files conform to TypeScript types
No build-time validation of cache JSON against expected schemas
No startup check in any API route that validates cache integrity before serving data
No snapshot tests, no fixture validation, no schema conformance tests
19.5.impact: If new cache files are created (e.g. adding a 4th wallet, new pattern categories, new persona fields), there is zero automated validation that they conform to expected types. A malformed cache file would only be discovered when the frontend crashes at runtime. Without tests, any cache regeneration or migration is a blind manual operation.
19.5.mitigation: Add a `validate-cache.ts` script that reads all cache JSON files and asserts they match expected TypeScript interfaces (using Zod schemas or manual type guards). Run it as a pre-build step (`npm run validate-cache` in `prebuild`). Add Playwright fixture tests that verify the app renders correctly with the current cache data.

summary: Alter Ego is a greenfield hackathon project with no upgrade infrastructure whatsoever. The most critical gaps: (1) the seed script referenced by both ARCHITECTURE.md and cache.ts does not exist, making cache regeneration impossible; (2) cache loading uses blind `JSON.parse(...) as T` casts with zero runtime validation, so type changes silently corrupt runtime behavior; (3) no migration tests exist to validate cache integrity. The Vercel deploy is linked but never completed (auth blocked). For a single-dev demo these are acceptable, but any productionization would require: a real seed script, Zod-based cache validation, a `cacheVersion` field, and a CI/CD pipeline.
